govdocs-archive_org-nsia-TammEdwardAJudg: A newspaper book review takes up a book about FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover and the Warren Commission. The file is cataloged under Judge Edward A. Tamm's name. The review text itself is heavily garbled, because the original two-column newspaper layout was hard to scan. Even damaged, it shows how books linking Hoover to the Kennedy inquiry were received and argued over in print.
podcast-dannyjones-leBR4jtRYDg:
Explorer Luke Caverns joins Danny Jones to report a lost Maya city found in the jungles of Central America. The episode title calls it a Mayan Atlantis just found. Caverns works old sites in the field and films his treks.

Caverns tells how the site was found and what the team saw once they cut in. He lays out the scale of the ruins and why he thinks the city was a hub. Jones asks what proof will win over the doubters. Listeners get a fresh field tale of loss and find. The library keeps the talk as an archive record of the claim.
podcast-joerogan-vtxyvD58eDg:
Vice President JD Vance joins Joe Rogan for episode 2526 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Vance rose from a hard Ohio start to the vice presidency. A sitting vice president on a podcast is a rare thing in US life.

Vance and Rogan roam across his life, the Hillbilly Elegy years, and the road to power. They talk faith, family, trade, and the wars the US funds abroad. Rogan keeps the tone loose and long, as his show does. Listeners get the man off script at full length. The library keeps the episode as a record of a rare political talk.
podcast-joerogan-tsu2-I2q6dg:
Episode 360 of the Joe Rogan Experience is Graham Hancock's classic early sit-down, a talk that shaped both men's futures. Hancock laid out his lost-civilization theory years before streaming made him a household name. Rogan gave him hours when mainstream shows gave him minutes.

Hancock connects flood myths, ancient monuments, and his claim of a wiped-out advanced culture. The talk ranges over the same ground as his banned TED appearance, at far greater length. Rogan asks the questions that later Hancock visits would refine into a saga. For fans of ancient mysteries, this is where the Rogan chapter began.
doe-osti-3001435-management-and-operatio: Oak Ridge National Lab got its management text, and this DOE report covers the operations. The pages detail the findings. The lab folks get their record. The lab was ORNL. The record was lab. The operations were detailed. The record was ORNL.
